Public Comments

  4. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. RECOGNITION OF WOMAN OF IMPACT AWARD FOR COMMUNITY SERVICES
  DR. CHASITY JENNINGS-NUNEZ

  Vice Chair Goto to present Chair Jennings-Nunez with a certificate of recognition for
  the San Gabriel City Council for her reception of the AD49 Women of Impact-
  Community Service Award.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the HEAR Commission receive and file this discussion item.

HEAR Commission Regular Meeting Agenda – March 28, 2023
   B. GUEST SPEAKER- LA COUNTY COMMISSION ON HUMAN RELATIONS

  The LA County Commission on Human Relations will present numbers specific to the
  San Gabriel area. The organization distributes the LA County Hate Crime Report
  annually so that they can track trends and develop potential solutions.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the HEAR Commission receive and file this discussion item.

  C. COMMISSION REORGANIZATION

  As part of the annual Commission reorganization process the Commission will select
  the new Chair and Vice-Chair for the HEAR Commission. Staff will present the options
  available to the Commissioners before a vote is taken.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the HEAR Commission select a Chair and Vice Chair for the
  Commission.

  D. DISCUSSION OF EQUITY VS EQUALITY

  Vice Chair Goto will present the differences between equity and equality.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the HEAR Commission receive and file this discussion item.

  E. FINALIZE AND APPROVE 2023 ANNUAL WORKPLAN

  Commission members to develop a 2023 Annual Workplan to guide the
  commission’s work throughout 2023.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the HEAR Commission finalize and approve the 2023 annual
  workplan.

  F. 2023 MENTAL WELLNESS EXPO PLANNING

  Commission members to continue planning the 2023 Mental Wellness Expo,
  scheduled for Sunday, October 1, 2023.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff members have the opportunity to address the Commission and public on matters

   MINUTES OF TUESDAY, FEBRUARY 28, 2023
  MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL
  HUMAN EQUITY, ACCESS, AND RELATIONS (HEAR) COMMISSION

CALL TO ORDER

Chair Jennings-Nuñez called the regular meeting of the HEAR Commission to order at 6:38 p.m.
on Tuesday, February 28, 2023, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San
Gabriel, California, 91776.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Commissioner Brenhaug.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Michelle Brenhaug, Cathie Chavez-Morris, Eric Chen, Viki Goto, Jorge
  Herrera, Chasity Jennings-Nuñez and Riaz (Rick) Khan

Commissioners Absent:  None

ANNOUNCMENTS

Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Manager, provided information for the public on
how to submit comments, and how to request meeting agendas. If you wish to address the HEAR
Commission, e-mail all public comments to HEARCommission@sgch.org.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  A motion was made by Vice Chair Goto and seconded by Commissioner Chen to
  remove agenda item 4D.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 7-0-0 as follows:
  Ayes: Brenhaug, Chavez-Morris, Chen, Goto, Herrera, Jennings-Nuñez, Khan
  Nays: None

HEAR COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  FEBRUARY 28, 2023
   Abstain: None

  2. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Andrew, longtime resident, commented on a Facebook post that was posted by Interim
  Chief Nakamura offering condolences to the family of Tyre Nichols. He stated that a
  member of the HEAR Commission left a reply that he believed to be disrespectful to the
  Chief and police officers.

  Jackie Borja requested that all the commissions be included in the Recreation Guide
  calendar page. Additionally, she noted that one of the QR codes for public comment did
  not work. She wanted to commend Chair Jennings-Nuñez for organizing a fun-filled art
  exhibit in honor and memory of her father, and in celebration of Black History Month at
  Blossom Market Hall.

  3. ACTION ITEMS

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A motion was made by Commissioner Herrera and seconded by Commissioner
  Khan to approve the minutes of the HEAR Commission Regular Meeting for
  January 24, 2023.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 5-0-2 as follows:
  Ayes: Brenhaug, Goto, Herrera, Jennings-Nuñez, Khan
  Nays: None
  Abstain: Chavez-Morris, Chen

  4. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. DISCUSSION OF APPROVED 2022 ANNUAL WORKPLAN
  Chair Jennings-Nuñez presented the item.

  The Commission discussed the Youth Ambassador program’s timeline,
  requirements, and deadlines. The deadline for submissions would be April 1st,
  however, there will be an extension if the minimum of 4 applicants is not met. A
  special meeting will be held before the April commission meeting for interviews.

  Public Comment: None

HEAR COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  FEBRUARY 28, 2023
   B. 2023 MENTAL WELLNESS EXPO PLANNING
  Commissioner Brenhaug presented the item.

  The Commission would like to allocate funds for translation equipment to use at
  the workshops. They are requesting a budget of $2,000 for the event and hope to
  receive additional sponsorships.

  The Commission will divvy up responsibilities as follows:
  • Marketing & Elected Officials Lead (Commissioner Chavez-Morris)
  • Raffle Lead (Commissioner Herrera)
  • Outreach Lead (Commissioner Chen)
  • Activity Lead (Commission Brenhaug)
  • Workshop Lead (Vice Chair Goto)
  • Exhibitor Lead (Commission Khan)
  • Volunteer Lead (Chair Jennings-Nuñez)

  Public Comment: None

  C. 2023 FINALIZE AND APPROVE 2023 ANNUAL WORKPLAN

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez presented the item.

  The Commission would like to organize a Safe Space campaign during PRIDE
  month (June) this year instead of a job fair.

  Commissioners discussed offering translations for meetings so that more
  members of the community can be informed.

  Data collection from the police department will be added under internal
  partnerships on the workplan.

  The Commission discussed adding a workshop for seniors regarding spam
  prevention.

  The Commission is interested in inviting speakers regarding environmental
  health, climate change and LGBTQIA+.

  City Manager Lazzaretto provided information regarding the recruitment process
  for Chief of Police. The Commission asked if the public would have the
  opportunity to ask questions. Commissioners also inquired if there would be
  language regarding experience working with a diverse community.

  Commission would like to push the accessible playground item to the
  Community Services Commission.

HEAR COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  FEBRUARY 28, 2023
   The Commission will have to put a hold on organizing an event for United
  Against the Hate to focus on other items.

  5. COMMISSION REPORTS

  Vice Chair Goto announced there will be a joint meeting on March 2 nd with City
  Council and Planning Commission regarding affordable housing. She also
  congratulated Chair Jennings-Nuñez on her art exhibit. She wanted to recommend
  a PBS documentary series, Fight the Power: How Hip Hop Changed the World. Vice
  Chair Goto shared information regarding the Michelson Spark Grants for Digital
  Equity.

  Commissioner Khan attended a health fair in Pomona, he would like to add
  something similar in the future.

  Commissioner Herrera attended Chair Jennings-Nuñez’s art exhibit and the San
  Gabriel Lunar New Year Celebration. He also participated in a speech and debate
  competition in Montebello in support of Gabrielino High School students.
  Commissioner Herrera shared that he held his 2nd community clean up in south
  San Gabriel, he thanked Manager Morales-Stevens for the use of equipment.

  Commissioner Chavez-Morris announced that March is Women’s History Month.
  She invited residents to attend an event, Women’s Career & Wellness Expo hosted
  by her employer, Los Angeles Department of Water & Power, on March 11.

  Commissioner Chen is thankful to be a part of the commission.

  Commissioner Brenhaug welcomed new commissioners Chen and Chavez-Morris.

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez thanks everyone who made it to her event and announced
  that she received the Proclamation from the City for Black History Month.

  6. STAFF COMMENTS
  Manager Morales-Stevens stated that the commission reorganization will be held at the
  next commission meeting.

  7. ADJOURNMENT

  Chair Jennings-Nuñez adjourned the meeting at 8:48 p.m.

  Next regular meeting is scheduled in person for Tuesday, March 28, 2023 at 6:30 p.m.

HEAR COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES  FEBRUARY 28, 2023

  Youth Ambassador 2023-2024 Application

 The purpose of the HEAR Commission is to advance and advocate for equity, access, diversity,
 social justice, safety, mutual appreciation, increased cultural competency, positive inter-group
 relations and respect for all members of the San Gabriel community.

The San Gabriel HEAR Commission Youth Ambassadors will:

  •  Work directly with the San Gabriel HEAR Commissioners serving as youth ambassadors
  and gaining hands-on community level work experience.
  •  Develop leadership skills through monthly HEAR Commission meetings focused on
  strengthening youth voice on issues related to human equity, access and relations.
  •  Learn about various equity and access issues impacting San Gabriel city residents and on
  how the HEAR commission and the various departments within the City of San Gabriel
  work to address them.
  •  Advise and make appropriate recommendations regarding issues of special interest to
  youth within the City of San Gabriel and help guide the work of the HEAR commission
  and city departments.

Dear Community Leader,

The City of San Gabriel’s Human Equity, Access and Relations (HEAR) Commission is
hosting the San Gabriel Mental Wellness Expo on October 1, 2023 from 12:00pm-3:00pm
at the Grapevine Arbor. The event will consist of informational booths, demonstrations,
giveaways, breakout sessions, and resources.

The purpose of the HEAR Commission is to advance and advocate for equity, access,
diversity, social justice, safety, mutual appreciation, increased cultural competency,
positive inter-group relations and respect for all members of the San Gabriel community.
Collectively, the commission determined the need for additional resources and programs
specifically geared toward mental health.

In support of the event we are calling on local community organizations to take part by
hosting a community booth. The City will provide an 8’ table, 2 chairs and a canopy. We
ask that you provide information on what resources or programs your organization has
to offer and encourage you to have giveaways and/ or an interactive component to
engage the participants.

If you are interested in participating in this event, please complete the attached
application and return it via mail or email at your earliest convenience in order to reserve
your space. If you have any questions or concerns, please feel free to contact me at
mmoralesstevens@sgch.org or 626-308-2875.

Thank you in advance for your support.

Sincerely,

Matthew Morales-Stevens
Community Services Manager
HEAR Commission Staff Liaison

March 28, 2023

To Whom It May Concern,

The City of San Gabriel’s Human Equity, Access and Relations (HEAR) Commission is hosting the
San Gabriel Mental Wellness Expo on October 1, 2023 from 12:00pm-3:00pm at the Grapevine
Arbor. The event will consist of informational booths, giveaways, demonstrations, breakout
sessions, resources and activities for kids and adults.

The purpose of the HEAR Commission is to advance and advocate for equity, access, diversity,
social justice, safety, mutual appreciation, increased cultural competency, positive inter-group
relations and respect for all members of the San Gabriel community. Collectively, the commission
determined the need for additional resources and programs specifically geared toward mental
health.

This event is a great opportunity for your business to get involved in our diverse San Gabriel
Community. With your in-kind donation the City of San Gabriel can provide an engaging,
impactful and enhanced event for our residents. We look forward to receiving all donations by
September 6, 2022. Please feel free to contact me at 626-308-2875 or mmoralesstevens@sgch.org
with questions or for more information.

Thank you for your consideration in donating to the San Gabriel Mental Wellness Expo.

Best regards,

Matthew Morales-Stevens
Community Services Manager
HEAR Commission Liaison
